newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - North Sea to plumb the dept.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - North Sea to plumb the dept.

text.p: European crudes are expected to weaken this week under pressure from lacklustre refinery margins, a closed arb to the U.S. and slow March buying.
Traders expected a muted level of activity early in the week because of IP Week trade functions in London.
"It's looking very weak. There's no arbitrage and a lot of early March crude to be placed," said a trader.
"I think Dated is doomed. It's going to head south," a further trader said.
Dated Brent and most other grades were expected to see lower differentials.
Only Forties looks better, but its value of Dated Brent +45 cents may not last if the U.S. major whose buying supported the grade last week decides it has all it needs.
Most traders said Dated Brent would continue at a discount to March, testing below the -20 cent level traded on Friday.
Wet Brent swaps have turned bearish, with this week talking almost at par with next week at around April +14 cents.

Indications of weak demand for Dated Brent were apparent in the five o'clocking on Friday of five of the seven cargoes nominated early March loading dates. In addition at least one late February cargo was hanging over the market.
Traders said March sales got off to a slow start, with few cargoes other than Forties finding homes late last week.
Urals dealers said weather closures of key Black Sea outlet Novorossiisk have had less impact so far this year than in previous winters, partly because of renewed Iraqi sales.
Despite Novorossiisk's closure for parts of February, refiners are not showing great interest in snapping up cargoes, they said.
International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates released last week showed January net former Soviet territory crude exports up 310,000 bpd on the month at 2.38 million bpd.
Iraq's SOMO is touting extra spot volumes to make up a shortfall in revenue from the U.N. oil-for-food plan caused by falling world prices.
Urals, at Brent -85 cents cif Med on Friday, was seen sinking toward a dollar discount.
Falling gas oil prices, which lost over $7 last week and 20 a tonne the week before, are expected to keep distillate-rich West African crudes under pressure.
Nigerian Forcados was looking particularly vulnerable with talk of a March 11-20 sale late last week at Dated brent +57 cents, down three cents from previous business.
"I don't see much downside on the lighter grades. We're going into the gasoline period and things should hold in their current range for now," a trader said.

Traders said the market would continue to focus on efforts to put together co-loaders of lighter material for the U.S. Gulf. With Venezuela supplying U.S. Gulf with sour volumes, West Africans are expecting greater demand for sweeter grades.
Any immediate extra Far East interest in the lighter Nigerian grades is seen as slow, with buyers declaring themselves comfortable for now.
-- William Maclean, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
